claim.quote: An analysis of 7 years of Milagro data performed on a 10-degree angular scale has found two localized regions of excess of unknown origin with greater than 12 sigma significance.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; journal reference as printed on the arXiv page: Phys.Rev.Lett.101:221101,2008.

name: Milagro finds two localized regions of excess 10-TeV cosmic rays

significance.quote: two localized regions of excess of unknown origin with greater than 12 sigma significance
significance.value: greater than 12 sigma significance (two localized regions); one region differs in spectrum from the isotropic cosmic-ray flux at 4.6 sigma

summary.plain: Seven years of Milagro data revealed two small patches of the sky with an excess of cosmic rays at about 10 TeV, whose origin is unknown. They are not gamma rays.
summary.technical: Analysis of 7 years of data on a 10-degree angular scale finds two localized excesses of unknown origin above 12 sigma, both inconsistent with gamma-ray emission; one has a different energy spectrum from the isotropic cosmic-ray flux at 4.6 sigma, consistent with hard-spectrum protons with an exponential cutoff and the most significant excess near 10 TeV.

title: Discovery of Localized Regions of Excess 10-TeV Cosmic Rays
why_it_matters: The abstract says potential causes are explored but no compelling explanation is found.
